audit_findings.title: Parent earnings are mixed with consolidated add-backs
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; 2025 consolidated D&A and amortization was $104.269 million, while $12.391 million of net income was attributable to NCI, versus the $103.8 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated add-backs increase OE although part belongs to NCI, while the starting income and share count represent only parent common holders.
audit_findings.evidence: Net income attributable to common shareholders decreased due to higher income attributable to non-controlling interests.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch, not merely a possible future risk. The exact overstatement cannot be derived without subsidiary-level add-backs, but the consolidated add-back pool exceeds the entire OE anchor and the filed NCI attribution is 11.9% of that anchor, making the issue reasonably capable of changing value.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild 2016-2025 OE using parent-attributable D&A, other add-backs, maintenance capex and distributable cash for each consolidated subsidiary and VIE; rerun all scenarios with the corrected series.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized interest can escape owner earnings entirely
audit_findings.magnitude: $38.176 million in 2025, equal to 36.8% of the $103.8 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Capitalized interest avoids current interest expense, can be excluded with growth capex, and its later depreciation can be added back, leaving financing costs absent from equity-level OE and growth reinvestment.
audit_findings.evidence: We capitalize interest costs relating to construction financing during the period of construction on energy assets we own.
audit_findings.explanation: The capitalization is demonstrated by the filing. Whether the valuation separately retained every dollar is not shown, but the stated method creates the identified escape route. The filed 2025 amount is large enough to alter the anchor and valuation conclusion materially.
audit_findings.action: Trace capitalized interest by year through energy-asset additions and depreciation, identify any explicit OE or reinvestment deduction, and rerun the valuation after deducting only amounts otherwise omitted.

audit_findings.title: Unaccrued SCE damages may be a claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $89 million, or $1.50 per diluted share and 5.6% of base equity value; incremental exposure is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any economic loss not already recognized through constrained revenue, withheld receivables, costs or liabilities reduces the equity bridge or future OE available to common holders.
audit_findings.evidence: It is at least reasonably possible we may incur an obligation to pay liquidated damages up to the maximum amount.
audit_findings.explanation: No liability is demonstrated: the claim remains disputed, Ameresco contests damages, and part of the amount has already been set off against milestone payments. Nevertheless, the filed maximum would reduce base value from $26.99 to approximately $25.49 per share if wholly incremental, so it is reasonably capable of affecting the valuation conclusion. Deducting the full amount without reconciliation could double count the loss.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $89 million maximum against constrained revenue, the approximately $110 million milestone receipt and set-off, receivables, withheld payments, recorded costs and liabilities; rerun the bridge only for the incremental parent-equity loss.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may perpetuate expiring tax subsidies
audit_findings.magnitude: identified 2025 benefit of $23.860 million: $12.160 million of Section 45Z credits plus the $11.700 million total income-tax benefit; the latter includes a filed $2.783 million Section 179D benefit and $17.699 million of energy-related tax credits
audit_findings.mechanism: Temporary credits and deductions raise anchor OE and, if carried into growth and terminal periods without expiry or reinvestment requirements, inflate operating PV.
audit_findings.evidence: However, the OBBB has ended the Section 179D deduction for construction projects that begin after June 30, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The benefits and statutory expirations are demonstrated. The durable adjustment remains unresolved because the tax benefit contains multiple items and some credits require additional capital investment. The identified 2025 benefit equals 23.0% of the OE anchor before replacing the tax benefit with a normalized positive cash-tax burden, making the issue material.
audit_findings.action: Build a year-by-year cash-tax and subsidy schedule for Section 179D, Section 45Z, ITCs and other credits, link investment-dependent benefits to required capital, and rerun OE through the terminal year using normalized post-expiry taxes.

audit_findings.title: Transient currency and derivative gains may remain in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $11.820 million pretax in 2025: $7.099 million of foreign-currency transaction gains plus $4.721 million of derivative gains, equal to 11.4% of the OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained in net income without normalization, nonrecurring gains raise anchor OE and are capitalized through forecast growth and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The decrease in other expenses, net is due to foreign currency transaction gains of $7.1 million versus losses of $3.8 million last year.
audit_findings.explanation: The gains are demonstrated, but their retention in the final OE adjustments is unresolved because no adjustment ledger was supplied. Their combined scale is reasonably capable of changing value; this finding is not a demonstrated valuation error until the OE schedule confirms they remain.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the 2025 OE adjustment ledger and underlying derivative classifications, remove any retained transient gains or substitute a documented through-cycle amount, then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The full cash add-back may not be distributable surplus
audit_findings.magnitude: $138.333 million added to the bridge, or $2.34 per diluted share and 8.7% of base value; $60.629 million, or $1.02 per share, was held in consolidated VIEs
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash required for working capital, covenants, project subsidiaries or NCI claims is operating or encumbered capital rather than a separate asset wholly available to parent common equity.
audit_findings.evidence: Working capital requirements can be susceptible to fluctuations during the year due to timing differences between costs incurred, the timing of milestone-based customer invoices and actual cash collections.
audit_findings.explanation: The full add-back is demonstrated, while the unavailable portion is unresolved. The filing identifies substantial working-capital demands, negative 2025 operating cash flow of $80.360 million, negative first-half 2026 operating cash flow of $71.813 million and material VIE cash. If none of the bridge cash were surplus, base value would fall by $2.34 per share and the 30% buy-below level would fall from $18.89 to about $17.25, making the classification material.
audit_findings.action: Obtain entity-level cash, covenant and distribution schedules; allocate VIE and NCI claims; estimate minimum operating cash from normalized project-cycle needs; and rerun the bridge using only cash distributable to parent common holders.
